column1: # OUTSIDE_SPITBOL_BASELINE.tsv -- dotnet: programs the ONE ORACLE itself does not run, so they are OUTSIDE
# the graded baseline and OUT OF THE DENOMINATOR. Lon 2026-09-08: the leaderboard divides by the programs
# SPITBOL runs clean, and a program SPITBOL cannot run is recorded per program with SPITBOL's own error AND
# a source check. Written coo 2026-09-08; test_snoflake_suite.sh is the shape.
# MEASURED, not declared: test_snobol4_dotnet_suite.sh decides UNSCR live each run from the oracle's own rc
# and stream, and cross-checks this file against what it saw, saying STALE or UNRECORDED aloud. UNGRADABLE.tsv
# mirrors this file row for row.
# ⭐ THREE DISTINCT REASONS THE ORACLE GIVES NO ANSWER, and they are not the same fact:
#   a fatal listing at rc=0 -- the oracle compiled and then stopped; a diagnostic is not an answer.
#   a BOM it cannot parse  -- the oracle never reached the program at all.
#   more than one END      -- the file is not one program, so there is nothing single to grade.
# Only the first is about the SNOBOL4 in the file. The other two are about the file.
# Oracle: /home/resources/x64/bin/sbl -bf. Columns: name <TAB> ORACLE_REFUSES|CONTAINER_OR_LIBRARY <TAB>
# does not run in SPITBOL: <error, file(line)>; source checked <date> (<who>): stmt <line> <source> -- <why>
# ⭐ CEO-1344 (the coo 2026-09-28): a run-time FATAL BLOCK at rc=0 is an ANSWER -- the oracle's block on stdout, graded through the
# rendered SCRIP block and ALL.mask -- so 1brc.sno (ERROR 121 at stmt 56) and asgn1.sno (ERROR 038 at stmt 5) LEFT this record: they are in the baseline, graded by
# test_snobol4_dotnet_suite.sh's FATAL_GRADED arm. expr_parser_stub.sno stays (ERROR 248 is the CSNOBOL4 feature its EXCLUDED row names). The
# BOM rows stayed (until CEO-1352, next): the oracle never reaches those programs, which is a different fact from a program the oracle runs and stops.
# CEO-1352 (the ceo 2026-09-28, hq_snobol4 landing): the five BOM programs (SourceLines001-003, Test, Test2) LEFT this record -- the
# leading UTF-8 BOM was stripped ONCE in the repo (CEO-544/571 precedent, recorded in _PROVENANCE.md), so both engines read the same
# bytes and the oracle answers them.
expr_parser_stub.sno
